answer: Distinct-Root Identity Quota. Each identity earns standing only through independently rooted activity: its first transactions must form a disjoint ancestry path, and merged paths pay a crossover toll proportional to shared history. A grove of accounts sharing one tree pays the toll on every merge. The bridge rule lets newcomers cross cheaply once; recrossing under a new key is blocked by path memory. The delta charged per fresh identity equals the median earned standing of its claimed roots, so mass fabrication costs full standing per head, not a discount.
